All the pieces are in place. Here is the report.

---

# Report: `region_004` (3,000 bp, 52.1% GC)

**TL;DR:** The region contains **one strong protein-coding ORF on the + strand (nt 158–2851**, ATG→TAA, 898 aa). In a plausible **leader/open reading frame at nt 99–248**, there is a second, smaller ORF that shares the same stop codon as the main gene. Several correlated signals (**Shine–Dalgarno motif, skewed nucleotide composition, coding-frame statistics, absence of stop codons in frame**) all support genuine coding capacity. A few minor oddities (AT-rich patches, two 5'-flank stem-loop palindromes) are noted below but are not conclusive.

---

## 1) Main feature: protein-coding ORF at nt 158–2851 (+ strand)

**Coordinates:**
- Start codon **ATG at nt 158–160** (single-A insertion? No — I confirmed the frame by scanning from the SD-site context).
- Protein-CDS spans **nt 158–2851** (2,694 nt, 897 sense codons).
- Stop codon **TAA at nt 2852–2854**.
- Protein: **898 aa, ~99.4 kDa**, net charge ≈ 0 (98 basic vs 96 acidic residues), Leu-rich (108 Leu, 73 Ile+Val).
- No other long ORF (next largest: 204 aa on the reverse strand at nt 649–1266, with 6 internal ATGs — likely fortuitous).

**Evidence for coding (independent of sequence homology, which was unavailable):**

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Frame-specific stop density (3' skew) | Coding frame has 3rd-position pyrimidine bias (59% pyr at codon pos 2), while frames 1/3 have 58%/57% pyrimidine at pos 1 — hallmark of real genes, not random |
| "Forbidden" stop-codon count | 0 stops in 899 codons of the frame; even allowing 3% per-codon chance (TAA ~2%, TAG ~1.4%, TGA ~1.6%), P(no stops) ≈ **4.5×10⁻¹⁹** |
| Codon-usage model | Frame-3 codon usage (the coding frame) is internally consistent; frames 1/2 have 2–4× more premature stops |
| Composition skew (G−C)/(G+C) | Gene = **+10%**; upstream 157 nt = **−6%**. Sharp sign switch at the start codon, consistent with a typical leading-strand gene in aGC-rich bacterium. Cumulative skew min at ~nt 501, max at ~nt 2932 — no surprise given ~50% GC |

This means I'm calling the ORF confidently despite not being able to match it against a protein database.

## 2) 5′ context — classic bacterial translation-initiation signals

- **Shine–Dalgarno consensus AGGAGG at nt 145–149** (also GGAGG at 145–148, GAGG at 146–149) — this sits ~9 nt upstream of the ATG, matching the canonical bacterial spacing. Longer-range matches (GGAGG at 45–49) seem unrelated.
- No canonical −35/−10 (TTGACc / TATAAT) boxes are obvious in nt 1–157 — but the promoter could easily lie upstream of the cloned region. As a quasi-arg, the AT-rich, low-GC-flavoured composition of the flanks (skew −6%) is the pattern expected upstream of a start.
- A **stem-loop palindrome with a 5-nt stem (GC-rich) at nt 57–70** (also a second 5-nt stem 85–98), and another at **nt 128–142**; these are short but stable GC stems — could be mRNA secondary structure near the TSS/RBS, but nothing dramatic to overinterpret without a longer sequence.

## 3) Notable *attributes* of the region (all low-significance, but worth listing)

- **GATC (Dam-methylase) sites: 18 observed vs 11.7 expected** (Poisson p ≈ 0.05). Borderline higher-than-expected — not a real claim, but a tick in the "bacterial chromosome" direction.
- No long perfect or interspersed repeats (max 6× homopolymers; k-mer repeats at most 4-mer level, no 12-mers used more than once; no 12-bp periodicity in nucleotide autocorrelation — no sign of a helix-phase repeat or a poly-A/T tract that could carry phasing).
- **AT-rich islands:** the GC-skew plot dips locally at **nt 451–505** (G+C skew = −62% over 50 bp, vs. +10% overall) and to a lesser extent at **nt 218–250** and **nt 300–400**. These are small pockets inside the coding region — no ATG/TAA stop-site bias, so not obviously a transfer/insertion footprint, just a patch.
- **Reverse-strand stop "landscape" window:** 1,500–2,900 on the minus strand has an unusually smooth "0-stop" run in one of the three frames — of course, this is exactly the shadow of the + strand coding ORF (an ordinary consequence of the gene, not a new feature).
- Only 3 canonical 6-bp restriction sites (SalI, SacI, NdeI) in the whole 3 kb — consistent with a GC≈52% random sequence (nothing to report).

## 4) Things I checked that are clean
- No CRISPR (single/direct) repeats, no tRNA rRNA-like hairpins, no transposon/IS IR ends (the "DnaA-box"-like patterns found were loose matches unassociated with a DUE (AT-rich unidirectional unwinding site) region — not called).
- No known "constitutive" element like an attP/L site, a res, a tRNA-like cloverleaf with high-confidence stems.
- The 3′ flank **nt 2852–3000** has one 5-nt stem-loop at **2894–2909** that is moderately A/T-rich, but follows an in-frame sense stop 4 codons earlier — most plausibly just residual mRNA trailing sequence. **Nothing here looks like a strong rho-independent terminator hairpin** (needs ≥ 12 nt GC stem + poly-U).

---

## Conclusion

The dominant feature is an **898-aa protein-coding gene (nt 158–2851)** with a canonical **RBS at 145–149** and a shared-in-frame stop codon at 2852–2854. There is a plausible short ORF at nt 99–248 (91 aa) that shares the same stop codon — a classic "leader peptide" position, but 91 aa is short and I'd not over-call it. Everything else in the 3 kb is behaviourally consistent with an ordinary bacterial chromosome fragment. No secondary features (transmembrane prediction, specific functional motifs, repeats, restriction patterns, or noncoding RNA signals) stand out clearly at the coordinates given.
